name: Nullskin Doctrine — The Concealment Orthodoxy
creator: Attributed to stylist collective Vashti Okonkwo-Brennan & associates, Tier 3 Milwaukee Stack
description: A movement demanding that all chrome augmentations be covered with precision-matched dermaplastic panels, creating the illusion of an unmodified body. Adherents argue this is not shame but sovereignty — the body as private architecture, the augment as interior truth. At its peak, Nullskin practitioners could be identified only by the faint seam-lines at jaw, wrist, and shoulder, which became their own subtle status signal.
cultural_impact: Nullskin reframed augmentation concealment as an act of philosophical restraint rather than self-erasure, splitting the augmentation rights community and generating years of internal debate about visibility, pride, and the politics of passing.
controversy: Augmentation pride advocates — particularly the Ironwear and Chrome Day communities — condemned Nullskin as internalized chrome-shame dressed in philosophical language. Corponations quietly endorsed it, as concealed augments were easier to mandate and harder to modify illegally.
story_hooks: A character whose Nullskin panels are flawless discovers that a rival can identify them by a specific pressure-gait caused by a concealed leg augment — someone has been watching closely enough to know.
A Nullskin practitioner is outed when a scanner at a corponation checkpoint sees through their dermaplastic — the readout shows augmentations that were supposed to be off the registry.
A teenager in Tier 3 adopts Nullskin not for philosophy but to hide illegal chrome from their parents, and accidentally becomes a minor icon of the movement.
